headline: Evidence, Not Screen Time, Becomes EdTech's New Procurement Test
thesis: The Education Department's guidance is turning "does it work" into a formal purchasing requirement, even as campuses reckon with a live cybersecurity breach and students write their own rules for AI.
summary: The Department of Education's August 20 Dear Colleague letter is rippling into procurement practice: coverage from THE Journal, EdSurge, and MarketScale (aggregated via EdTech Digest) describes districts and vendors now expected to show "purpose, proof, and process" in edtech contracts, with usage metrics like log-ins no longer sufficient justification — a shift arriving as K-12 districts already juggle an average of 2,591 separate edtech tools. Cybersecurity stays urgent and concrete: Inside Higher Ed reports the University of Texas at San Antonio delayed the start of its fall semester after an attempted breach at the network edge, while EdTech Magazine covers community colleges centralizing security operations as EDUCAUSE's 2026 list ranks collaborative cybersecurity a top higher-ed priority. On AI governance, the center of gravity keeps shifting toward students and educators themselves: EdSurge and AASA report more than 130 student leaders from all 50 states approved the STUDENTS FIRST Act, a first-of-its-kind student-authored national AI policy framework, while ISTE's updated standards fold AI literacy into existing digital-citizenship indicators rather than building a separate track, and Brookings publishes companion pieces on AI surveillance risks and school AI councils. In higher ed policy, Inside Higher Ed tracks the Trump administration's new accreditation overhaul and continuing fallout from Secretary McMahon's reform push, alongside research questioning how equitable "meritocratic" admissions really are. On the standards and conference calendar, 1EdTech's September 1 discussion with NASWA on workforce development leads into its Learning Impact Europe conference in Thessaloniki, while Ed-Fi's summer AI working group continues examining what its data standard needs for an AI-driven ecosystem.
footnote: Compiled from 11 curated edtech sources · August 31, 2026 · Direct page fetches (WebFetch) were unreliable for several publishers this run, so items were sourced and dated via web-search indexing rather than live page verification in some cases; a few sources are represented by their most relevant recent or evergreen material where no article dated today could be confirmed.

themes.title: EdTech Procurement Gets an Evidence Requirement
themes.body: THE Journal, EdSurge, and MarketScale report the Education Department's August 20 guidance is turning "purpose, proof, and process" into a de facto procurement standard, with usage metrics like log-ins no longer enough to justify an edtech contract.

themes.title: A Live Breach Keeps Campus Cybersecurity Concrete
themes.body: Inside Higher Ed reports UT San Antonio delayed its fall semester start after an attempted network-edge breach, while EdTech Magazine covers community colleges centralizing security operations as EDUCAUSE ranks collaborative cybersecurity a top 2026 priority.

themes.title: Students Write Their Own National AI Policy
themes.body: EdSurge and AASA report over 130 student leaders from all 50 states approved the STUDENTS FIRST Act, a student-authored AI policy framework covering privacy, authentic learning, and human judgment, at Boston's America's Youth AI Festival.

themes.title: AI Literacy Folds Into Existing Digital-Citizenship Standards
themes.body: Rather than build a separate AI track, ISTE is updating existing indicators for safe, responsible, and innovative AI use, while its Google partnership rolls out educator-centered AI literacy training toward a goal of six million teachers.

themes.title: Higher Ed's Federal Policy Reset Keeps Widening
themes.body: Inside Higher Ed tracks the Trump administration's new accreditation oversight rule and continuing fallout from Secretary McMahon's reform push, alongside new research questioning how "meritocratic" elite-college admissions actually are.

themes.title: Fall Standards and Workforce Calendar Builds
themes.body: 1EdTech holds a September 1 discussion with NASWA on workforce development ahead of its Learning Impact Europe conference in Thessaloniki, while Ed-Fi's summer AI working group studies what its data standard needs for an AI-driven ecosystem.

arts.t: Department of Education Issues Long-Awaited Edtech Guidance for States and Districts
arts.s: New federal guidance reframes edtech evaluation around measurable learning outcomes rather than screen-time limits, while leaving rulemaking to states and districts.

arts.t: EdSurge Welcomes Top Journalists and Educators to Advisory Board
arts.s: EdSurge adds six new members, including journalists and education leaders, to its advisory board.

arts.s: A Dear Colleague letter from the Department's Office of Elementary and Secondary Education argues screen time shouldn't be the primary measure of whether edtech is good or bad.

arts.t: K-12 Technology Leaders Are Doing Too Much: 3 Ways to Reclaim Strategic Focus
arts.s: Argues K-12 IT and technology leaders are overloaded with responsibilities and offers strategies for narrowing focus back to core strategic priorities.

arts.t: New CoSN Report Offers Guidance on Responsible Technology Use in Schools
arts.s: CoSN's updated guidelines favor plain-language Responsible Use Agreements over traditional Acceptable Use Policies, built with student and family input.

arts.s: New research finds roughly two-thirds of students at top-50 private universities come from the top income quintile, questioning how meritocratic elite admissions really are.

arts.s: Rather than build a separate AI-specific track, ISTE updated existing digital-citizenship indicators to cover safe, responsible, and innovative AI use.

arts.t: ISTE+ASCD and Google Partner to Provide AI Literacy Training to Six Million U.S. Educators
arts.s: A multi-year partnership will deliver AI literacy training to six million K-12 and higher-ed educators nationwide.

arts.t: AI Surveillance in Schools Raises Safety and Equity Concerns
arts.s: Examines how AI-powered monitoring tools meant to protect students raise new questions about privacy, bias, and equitable enforcement.

arts.t: What We Still Don't Know About AI and Children's Relationships
arts.s: Surveys the open research questions about how children's use of conversational AI tools shapes social and emotional development.

arts.t: Enhancing Student Agency Through School AI Councils
arts.s: Argues schools should establish student-led AI councils so students act as co-designers of AI policy rather than passive recipients of top-down rules.

arts.t: The Next Phase of AI in Education Is About Stewardship
arts.s: Argues education's AI conversation is moving past adoption into stewardship — governance, oversight, and long-term responsibility for how the tools are used.

arts.t: Screen Time Debate Gets More Nuanced
arts.s: Covers the shifting conversation around student screen time as the Education Department reframes edtech evaluation around outcomes rather than hours logged.

arts.t: Shaping What's Next
arts.s: An interview with Dr. Sheryl R. Abshire on developing bold leaders, defending digital access, and keeping education focused on the future.
